newsitem.title: FRANCE: Toulouse air cargo traffic down 10 pct in Jan-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Toulouse air cargo traffic down 10 pct in Jan-Nov.

text.p: Air cargo traffic handled at Toulouse-Blagnac Airport in the first months of 1996 totalled 23,351 tonnes, a decrease of 10 percent on the same period last year, provisional figures from the airport authority showed.

While freight still shows a double-digit decline for the year so far, last month the airport handled 2,418 tonnes which represented a 12 percent increase on November 1995 and marked the first time this year that traffic had progressed on last year's levels, an authority official told Reuters.

The growth in airfreight last month was probably largely due to more traffic being carried on scheduled airline services from Bordeaux and a growing volume of shipments generated by aircraft manufacturers based at Toulouse, the official said.
Another factor may have been that some road freight was carried by air due to the French truckers'dispute at end-November, the official added.
In September 1996, United Parcel Service launched a weekday feeder flight between Lyon-Satolas and Toulouse with a two-tonne cargo capacity Beechcraft 1900 chartered from Air Littoral.
DHL Worldwide Express operates a nightly flight between Brussels and Toulouse using a six-tonne capacity Convair aircraft.
Toulouse also features on French express distributor, Jet Services' domestic airfreight network which operates BAe146 QC (quick change) aircraft.
Airfreight is also carried by airlines operating passenger services to and from Toulouse, notably the Air France group.
Between January-November 1996 postal traffic handled Toulouse Airport increased by four percent on the same period last year to 17,931 tonnes.
French airline, L'Aeropostale, carries overnight mail between its Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle hub and Toulouse using Boeing 737QC aircraft. Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44-171-542-7706 Fax +44-171-542-5017
